Well nowadays I, unfortunately, there’s a lot of franchises vying for that spot. But I think you’re spot on about the good will associated with it. I rewatched I think earlier this year after remembering them fondly from my childhood. And, well, I was sorely disappointed.

1. Raiders of the Lost Ark: what can I say about this that hasn't been said before. I love it the same reason everyone else loves it

2. Last Crusade: it feels like a proper sequel, while also exploring the back story. I dont think Indiana Jones needs a sequel, so much as it needs non-sequential stories of other adventures he goes on. Like how the  James Bond franchises works. Still, this builds on the mythology establish in the previous film while keeping with the in universe rules.

3. Temple of Doom: this movie is silly and does do the non-sequential adventure that I want to see in this franchise. It's definitely more childish, which holds it back some, but is still fun to watch. And while it doesn't keep in line with the judeo-christian mythology of the other 2 films, nothing contradicts it, which is more than I can say about the next film 

4. Crystal Skull: I actually liked Shia LaBeouf here, or at least, he's not as bad as everyone says. Also, this movie has a good villain and while overdose it with the CGI, the action is memorable and creative. There are two problems here. First, old Indiana Jones isn't fun to watch. Second including Aliens undermines the previous films. Now instead of Jesus and Moses being biblical figures, they are just guys who found alien tech, which is lame.

5. Dial Of Destiny: again, I liked the Waller-Bridge as the sidekick, I thought she was fine. But that's where the good ends. The villain was boring, the action was boring, Indiana Jones was even older than before and even more boring than before. And the time travel aspect just all felt pointless.

This is the first time I've ever encountered someone that said the TOD was good much less the best of the franchise. It might be easier to provide a ranking between 1 and 10 with 10 being the best and 1 being the worst.

* Raiders: 10 - one of my favorite movies of all time
* TOD: 4 - too much absurd too early in the movie. Lost my suspension of disbelief right at the beginning. And the Kali heart thing...sigh..
* Last Crusade: 6 - really isn't that bad and the supernatural nonsense is saved to the last.
* Crystal Skull: 1 - this one grows on me as the years go by...but in a bad way. 
* Dial of Destiny: 4 - not nearly as terrible as Crystal Skull, but still not fanatastic. Not a well put together script. Way too many threads left open.

My list:

1. Last Crusade
2. Raiders of the Lost Ark
3. Temple of Doom
4. Dial of Destiny

I think I've always liked Last Crusade more than Raiders of the Lost Ark, because of the wonderful father/son plot. There's just more going on than just a story about a relic. Connery and Ford are a wonderful pair and they are just so much fun to watch. 

Dial of Destiny was a lot better than I expected, but I can't rate it higher than Temple of Doom. Dial of Destiny just needed a tighter script and better editing. Some of the action scenes go on for way too long and you can tell they run out of steam, but then keep going ang going, while most of the excitement is already gone. However, I can appreciate the absolutely bonkers ending, that is completely unlike an Indiana Jones movie. There's a fine line that the movies usually do not cross, but Dial of Destiny goes there, and it was highly entertaining. I also appreciated how they reunited the old cast in a loving way. Most importantly, you can tell Ford is enjoying himself filming it. The happyness radiates from his face during all of this, and that makes it a far more enjoyable watch than I expected.

And that's all of the Indy movies rated!

It's still impressive that at 80 Ford was able to reprise Indy a final time. You can tell he had fun. It's a shame the film didn't do better but it seems to be doing quite well with the Blu-ray/4K sales so it may be enjoying something of a second wind, which is good.

Great movie: last crusade and raiders 
Good but heavy flaws: temple of doom 
Garbage but fond memories: crystal skull 
Garbage but people are too mean to it: dial of destiny 

Skull was the first Indie I watched and made me fall in love with the franchise being rather young I didn’t notice the flaws, almost immediately watched the first three and loved them all so much wasn’t till watching those did I notice the flaws in skull. Dial of destiny is a bad movie but PWB’s character is fun and I liked a lot of the initial story, yes the opening is too long and the time travel is beyond stupid and lots of other problems but I still want a PWB solo action adventure film after this

>"it really lacks the feeling of danger and threat the first two have in so much abundance. The constant barrage of gags, reducing Sallah and Brody to useless comic relief"

LOL the OP clearly lives in some alternate bizzaro universe. Temple features plenty of gross out gags, slapstick bits, a love interest who screams or whines throughout and animal comedy bits with elephants.

It at least still has a sense of danger to it and the villains are genuinely threatening. It's got it's share of humor but not at the expense of the tension unlike in TLC where it's non-stop gags. Brody and Sallah especially have a lot of embarrassing moments. Those two really stick out like a big sore thumb in that film.

"The rest are pretty run of the mill action-adventure movies."

While they weren't the absolute first, they were the ones to popularize the whole treasure hunting action-adventure genre.

Meh. I liked it a lot more than Crystal Skull.

See ya in twenty years.

We don't see the Thuggee villains until an hour into the movie. They're just one-dimensional evil zombies Indy has to defeat. At least the villains in TLC have some actual motivations and some dimension to them. We also get to see what's driving them into the story and why they're after the Grail as well. ToD never really does that with its villains. 

And TLC is non-stop gags? What do you call the emotional father-son stuff between Indy and Henry to be then? Or the Nazi book burning where Indy confronts Elsa, the tough and gritty boat chase in Venice or the big tank fight? There's a TON of serious emotional stuff there which you seem to conveniently ignore and cherry pick the comedy scenes. 

And I'm sorry but I fail to understand the issue with Brody and Sallah. We barely saw Brody in Raiders and sure, in Crusade he may have some humorous parts, but he still gets in moments to be tough and helpful. See him telling Donovan he's meddling with powers he can't comprehend, and by story's end, he's helping Indy fight the Nazis. Sallah had his comical parts in Raiders like screaming in fear when he sees the scary statue or when he sings when Marion kisses him. It's no different in TLC. 

And if you're going to pick out Brody and Sallah's comical parts, then you might as well mention ALL the stuff with Willie Scott, who is nothing more than over the top comic relief.

> The last one, to me isn’t even worth a casual watch.

After reading the introduction to this post, I wondered to how many people in r/TrueFilm have even seen “all five” movies about Indiana Jones (excluding anyone who saw one or both of the last two “for work,” ie a critic or someone who writes film criticism with an eye toward more than posting and sees many new releases).

I have difficulty imagining a poster here who would enjoy that exercise. It’s like ranking the movies of the *Pirates of the Caribbean* or *Ghostbusters* franchises. The sorts of elements that people often look for in film criticism as distinguishing markers are not present for the most part.

All of these criticisms precede the “unashamed, unapologetic” “defense” of *Temple of Doom*, which is orientalist hogwash. Why is it the clubhouse leader? Because OP saw it before other Indiana Jones movies. (“Five stars, I was at an advanced screening.”)

You can say the same thing about the Nazis in the other films. They're all pretty much just zombies aside from the big bads they're serving in their respective films. I always found Donovan a boring and uninteresting villain, which is of no fault of the actor. The character is just boring to me.

I'm not denying TOD has it's share of humorous moments including Willie, but it still takes the intense and serious parts seriously and the humor doesn't undermine the darker moments unlike in TLC. Weirdly, the humor in TLC actually gives the film a bit of a bipolar tone with the father/son storyline which is well-done but smack dab in the middle of a lot of the wacky elements of the film which give it this off-kilter feeling. Brody may not have had a big role in Raiders but there's nothing indicative of him being so buffoonish as he became in TLC, same with Sallah. His scream in Raiders seeing the statue was funny, yes, but not something that takes you out of the film or takes away from the seriousness of the scene in which it occurs.

Not exactly and I'm not talking about the Nazis themselves, but the actual villains with names. Because in Raiders and Crusade, they establish who Belloq and Donovan are before the main story takes place and how they relate to Indy. It's established what their motivations are and what they hope to accomplish. They also establish the supporting villains like Toht, Dietrich, Vogel, Elsa and Kazim, the leader of the Cruciform Sword, as well and we get a sense of what drives them into the story.   
  
With ToD, we don't get introduced to Mola Ram until an hour into the movie and he's given no real motivation other than him being EVIL and wanting to overthrow other religions, which is pretty vague stakes. 

You seem to forget how ToD features a story about a starving village on the brink of death, an evil cult practicing human sacrifice and child slavery, yet don't find an issue with the slapstick humor, gross out gags, comic relief love interest and animal comedy stuff clashing with all that? The movie's action sequences are also over the top (see: the life raft escape, the mine car jumping over the chasm, Short Round doing kung fu on grown adult henchmen and the Thuggee's arrows missing Indy). 

Again, Brody and Sallah aren't as buffoonish as you make them out to be because they're also helping Indy fight back against the Nazis and when the movie needs them to be serious (see: the climax where Henry's been shot), they're pretty serious! Compare this to Willie Scott who's a cartoon bimbo throughout and only becomes useful on ONE occasion when she punches the Thuggee henchman during the mine car chase.
This is the proper offer and I would assume is the most widely accepted.

In all fairness, TOD was trying to be a completely different movie from Raiders. Mola Ram may not be that well-developed a villain but he's at least very menacing and threatening, unlike Donovan who's so bland. Donovan has no real motivation either aside from wanting to live forever, which itself is also a pretty run of the mill motivation.

Never said TOD doesn't have over the top stuff and it's share of gags, but it was never at the expense of the tension and the more serious aspects were never undermined. People always like to rag on the raft stunt, but give a pass to the equally over the top stuff in TLC like the centuries-old Grail Knight, the plane in the tunnel, the petroluem-filled catacombs waters never igniting from Indy's lit torch, etc. and young Indy escaping off of a moving train using a magic box he never used before and had no knowledge of how. Brody and Sallah may be more helpful by the end of the film but it doesn't change how cartoonish they were throughout so much else of the film. Then there's the pen ink squirting in the eye, which while funny was something that took away from the tension of the tank sequence, which was a highlight of the film.

You don't find wanting to live forever to be at least some form of motivation at least? It's at a plausible thing for a villain to desire. What exactly does Mola Ram hope to accomplish in getting all five stones to take over the world? That's never explained in the film. 

That stuff in ToD is VERY much in expense at the serious aspects because it's hard to take a story about child slavery and a human sacrificing cult seriously when there's a loud shrill love interest screaming and whining throughout, gross out (and also racist) gags like the monkey brain feast and other campy stuff throughout. 

Maybe people give all that fantastical stuff in Crusade a pass because: a.) it has an emotional father-son story to give it heart and balance it out, b.) still fits tonally within the story about two estranged men seeing their differences and working together, c.) it's more interesting than ToD's vague sacred stones which are never explained.

Living forever or world domination, at the end of the day neither is a terribly deep motivation. We never find out what Donovan plans to do when he lives forever, either.

The criticisms of TOD being racist are so tiresome and reek of looking for something to complain about. If TOD is racist then so are the other films, as Germans as Nazis and Russians as Soviets aren't terribly positive portrayals of people of those nationalities, either. Neither are island natives portrayed as savages as we saw in Raiders and KOTCS. TOD has it's share of gross-out gags but at least it fit with the film's Horror theme. Willie's screaming at least fits considering what she's experiencing and witnessing, far more than Jones, Sr. shouting "Junior!" every other moment.

I fail to see how all of the over the top and outlandish stuff in TLC fits in with a father/son storyline. Is that somehow supposed to make it less over the top? Because it doesn't and if anything makes the film feel very off-kilter. At least TOD had that comic book feel to it where it's more OTT elements fit, whereas TLC it just feels very off. Balancing something serious like a father and son story with all of the wacky stuff present in the film makes it feel tonally off the wall. Sure the raft in TOD is unrealistic but it at least shows how Indy is quick-thinking to escape from a life-threatening situation where he's mere moments away from dying. I don't see how the raft is too unrealistic but a centures-old Grail Knight is just fine.

At the time of ToD's release, there wasn't much representation for India/South Asia in mainstream movies and TV shows, so Temple's incorrect portrayals of the Indian characters eating chilled monkey brains and worshipping Kali like a Hindu satan was not only culturally inaccurate, but also offensive and irresponsible of the filmmakers. That there were German Nazis and Russian Soviets is a poor defense because back then at least Germans and Russians had plenty other representations besides those portrayals. 

How is Jones Sr. saying Jr. not fit with the story? He's an academic professor out of his depth in an action adventure and it fits with what his character is about. 

Again dude, you're being very vague in calling TLC for it's so-called "Wacky elements". I just mentioned all the serious stuff like the father-son emotional stuff, the Nazi book burning, Kazim is killed, the scene where Henry thinks Indy has died, the entire final climax where Henry's been shot and Elsa falls to her death which are all quite serious. Even if there's humor, it's not done in some silly fashion like Willie screaming, or monkey brains and elephant antics. TLC has the emotional stuff to balance it out.

Yeah but Germans as Nazis and Soviets as Russians isn't any less of a negative and harmful stereotype. Calling the film racist reeks of looking for something to complain about. Not all of the Indian characters were depicted as that, only the Thuggees, meant to show how evil they were. If TOD is racist for it's portrayal of Indian people, then the other films are also racist in their own way. Yet somehow only TOD is guilty of that.

Did Jones, Sr. have to constantly say "Junior!" throughout so much of the film? And in such a comedic fashion to boot? The film is full of so many gags and other OTT, silly stuff peppered throughout that really undermines the whole tone for me. As for the stuff you mentioned, the film gets quite good during the third act and the third act with the Path of God, the Leap Of Faith, etc. all feel like vintage Indy. But there's so much goofy, wacky stuff present in the film's first two acts and the OTT stuff mixed in with the more serious aspects gives the film a bit of a bipolar feeling and it's more campy elements really don't mesh well, IMO. I haven't even mentioned the revolving fireplace bit, Indy tumbling down the steps in a Three Stooges-esque fashion, the librarian using the boom stamp at the same time as Indy smashing the floor tiles, etc. I'm not denying TOD has it's share of humors and gags, but not nearly to the extent of TLC and TOD has it's darker, more Horror-like aspects to balance it out. TLC's tone through and through is very light and comedic, at times bordering on campy, and then it shifts for the third act to get more serious.

I'll have to respectfully disagree with much of what you're saying, but one thing we can agree even if we don't exactly see eye to eye on the film is it's still good. I never once said TLC is a bad film or one I don't enjoy. I've got my issues with it, but I by no means dislike it. It's a film I can sit through and enjoy just fine, even if it isn't my go-to Indy film.

They saw TOD first. That's a big factor in determining favourite entry in a franchise. A friend of mine thinks Alien 3 is the best alien movie which I found extraordinary...until he mentioned that he saw it before Alien/Aliens.

Obviously it doesn't apply in every case but it happens way more than random chance that a viewer will "overrate" the first movie they see in a series (Vs the average perception). It sort of makes sense that this would be so.

raiders - it’s the greatest movie ever made.

last crusade - it has the spirit and nostalgia but it is so fucking ridiculous and goofy and unserious that it’s almost a parody. but the last act is perfect.

temple - people hate on it but it’s good. it just takes place in one location for a majority of the film so it feels smaller in scale. and then the minecart chase is way too fucking long. i checked my phone the last time i watched it because it was taking so god damn long to end that entire cave fight sequence. it feels like a third of the runtime. so the pacing is a real issue here. but i love how it more closely resembles the serials that inspired it than any of the other ones really do

crystal skull - not good but not as bad as you remember. it’s goofy and unserious but it still has some of the indy heart. shia does a fine job in this people just don’t like his character. to think people hated this enough to spawn a cartoon of indy being raped on south park, naively thinking it couldn’t get any worse.

dial of destiny - insultingly bad film dragging the corpse of a beloved character around the world and fucking him over and shitting on him and torturing him the entire time. indy is a bystander in his own movie while the “lead” acts as a villain the entire film then does a dreadfully unconvincing change of heart where she turns to hero… at the end of the film when the damage is done and it’s way too late. and then she fucks over indy one last time by ignoring his wishes and doing whatever she wants anyway. if you’re gonna make an antihero, maybe make them likeable. unwatchable dogshit. a commercial made to sell tickets to the most expensive bomb of all time. pigslop for drooling pop culture nerd re7ards.
